ImageDescription.value:
In early October, the 14 Female Food Hero finalists entered a "Big-Brother" style reality TV show - a TV village modelled on the traditional Tanzanian rural village. The finalists will be filmed here for 2 weeks, with the audience voting by SMS for the winner.

The finalists will be joined by 36 young people from urban areas around the country. The women farmers will set daily tasks from their own lives – cultivating vegetables, looking after cattle, or setting up a small village business – which the young city dwellers will need to complete in order to earn a living and put food on the table. In the “diary room" they will get chance to record and share their views with politicians and decision makers.

Find out more about the TV village: oxf.am/JvY

Categories.value: Delta, Colorado|PD USDA|Flickr images missing SDC creator|United States photographs taken on 2012-07-18|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from U.S. Department of Agriculture Flickr stream|U.S. Department of Agriculture Flickr files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot|Flickr images missing SDC published in

ImageDescription.value:
Saw "Richard" Peter, Naw Susu, and their sons watch television in the living room of the first home that own in the United States, in Delta, Colorado, on July 18, 2012. They are an ethnic minority Karen refugee family from Myanmar (formerly known as Burma).

They started a new life of home ownership in the United States, thanks to the Guaranteed Home Loan program from USDA Rural Development.

When Peter, an agricultural worker, and his family first arrived in Delta, they lived in Alta de la Montana, a new multi-family 41-unit rental housing complex for low-income farm laborers and their families. Later, Peter started a new job with better pay, and he felt it was time to stop renting and get a home of his own. Initially, he had concerns about whether his credit would be good enough to qualify for a mortgage. He worked with Cindy Webster from Republic Mortgage, a local lender participating in the USDA Rural Development Guaranteed Home Loan Program, and learned that his credit was even better than he thought. Webster helped him throughout every stage of the application process, and he was subsequently approved for the loan. The family moved into its new home in the summer of 2012. It will give Peter’s two sons a sense of permanency, and they will also benefit from educational opportunities at nearby good quality schools. USDA Photo by Lance Cheung.

Credit.value: 20120718-RD-LSC-1163
